name: Fluent 2 Inspired
description: An independent interpretation of Fluent 2's public design principles: 4px controls and cards (borderRadiusMedium) and 8px dialogs (borderRadiusXLarge), circular badges, neutral strokes on controls and quieter ones on rules, its elevation ramp at its source's values, each level an ambient layer and a key at its Darker shadow pair, 20% and 24% (cards at shadow28 with no stroke of their own, prominent surfaces and overlays at shadow64, as microsoft/fluentui's packages/tokens/src/utils/shadows.ts and alias/lightColor.ts give them), 32px controls with 12px padding, an acrylic still (a luminosity sheen from each surface's top edge over a material grain), and decelerating motion that never nudges. It ships no official component, token file, icon, or font.

provenance.attribution: Keyur Golani, after Fluent 2's public principles. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft.
provenance.derivation: The reviewed prototype's fluent recipe, with its --appearance-* references read as --color-*, and the contract's signature-fill and emphasis-glow at the fallback language's values.

fallbacks: Under reduced transparency, without backdrop-filter, in forced colors, and in print, surfaces render opaque and the backdrop blur is 0.
Under reduced motion, transforms and emphasis stop and entrances and exits fade; a paused boundary and print are instant.
In forced colors, the material is a solid surface, and shadows and texture drop.
caveats: Translucent surfaces with a backdrop blur cost paint time on slower devices, and read less clearly over busy content.
A decorative gradient texture sits behind surfaces.
Its lift barely shows in dark: the shadow role is black in every set, and a dark ground hides it, so in dark its levels separate by fill. A mode-aware shadow role is post-surge.

Ships opaque: its approved 92% translucent surfaces fall under the contrast targets with its texture over a black or white backdrop, so its surfaces are 100% opaque, and only a dialog's backdrop is blurred. This supersedes the translucency caveats above.

tokens.surface-material: linear-gradient(color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-surface-default) 92%, transparent), color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-surface-default) 92%, transparent))
tokens.shadow-card: 0 0 8px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-shadow) 20%, transparent), 0 14px 28px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-shadow) 24%, transparent)
tokens.shadow-overlay: 0 0 8px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-shadow) 20%, transparent), 0 32px 64px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-shadow) 24%, transparent)
tokens.shadow-raised: 0 0 8px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-shadow) 20%, transparent), 0 32px 64px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-shadow) 24%, transparent)
tokens.texture: linear-gradient(color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-canvas) 28%, transparent), transparent 2.5rem), radial-gradient(circle, color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-text-primary) 12%, transparent) 0 0.5px, transparent 0.75px)
